Govindānanda
------------------------------------------
The medieval Hindu society (and, to a considerable extent, the modern Hindu society too) is regulated by the smṛtis, the धर्मशास्त्रस्, the पुराणस् and the निबन्धस् (digests) in its performance of rituals and some sacraments. Govindā-नन्द who flourished during the period A. D. 1500-1540 (exact dates not known) was an important author of निबन्धस्. He was a Vaiṣṇava and probably lived in Bāgri in the Medinīpur (Midnapur) district of West Bengal.
He wrote eleven works in all, of which mention may be made of the following: Dānakaumudī, Śuddhikaumudī, Śrāddha-kaumudī, and Varṣakriyākaumudī.
These works, respectively deal with the subjects of दान (gifts), शुद्धि (purifi-catory rites), śrāddha (obsequial rites) and festivals observed throughout the year.

Govardhana
(‘that which helps in the prosperity of the cows’)
------------------------------------------
Govardhana is a small hillock situated about 25 kms. (16 miles) from the town मथुरा in Uttar Pradesh.
When कृष्ण was living in Vṛndāvana, he found that one day all the elders of the village were busy preparing for the annual festival of Indramaha (vide Viṣṇupurāṇa 5.10.16) involving the worship of इन्द्र, the king of the gods in हेअवेन्. With a view to demolishing the pride of इन्द्र, कृष्ण advised his foster-ड़थेर् नन्द and the other elders of the village to abandon it and worship instead, the गोवर्धन hillock as also the cows and the bulls. It is they that were protecting and sustaining them. His suggestion was gladly accepted and duly implemented.
Enraged by this act of ‘arrogance’ on the part of कृष्ण, इन्द्र, the lord of clouds and rain, retaliated by creating an unprecedented deluge. However, the boy कृष्ण lifted up the गोवर्धन hillock with one hand, held it like an umbrella and protected the people of the village who took shelter beneath it. इन्द्र realised his folly and the true nature of कृष्ण as विष्णु himself. After apologising and worshipping him, he left for his heavenly abode. Since then कृष्ण came to be known as ‘Govardhana-giridhārī’ (‘one who lifted the गोवर्धन hill’), ‘Govinda’ (‘one who protected the cows’) and ‘Upendra’ (‘one who was above or superior to इन्द्र’).
The गोवर्धन hillock near मथुरा is about 6.5 kms. (4 miles) in length and not very high. Pilgrims who visit it sometimes do ‘parikrama,’ i.e., circumambulation, as per the directions given in some smṛtis and पुराणस्.
A ceremonial worship of the hillock (called ‘Govardhanapūjā’) is generally held on Kārttika-śukla-pratipad (first day of the bright fortnight in the month of Kārttika, generally in November), the day being known as ‘Balipratipadā’ also. Worship of cows and bulls is an important aspect of this festival.
In other places, the worship is done to a replica of the hillock.
See also ANNAKŪṬA.

Govardhana Maṭha
------------------------------------------
One of the pioneering works done by शङ्कर (A. D. 788-820) is the establishment of four maṭhas or monasteries in four cardinal places of India to spread Vedic religion and Advaita philosophy. They are: the Kālikā मठ at द्वारका in the west, Gujarat; the ज्योतिर् मठ near Badarī in the north, in Uttaranchal; the गोवर्धन मठ at Pūrī in the east, in Orissa and the शारदा मठ at Śṛṅgeri in the south, in Karnataka.
मठ.jpg" src="http://eoh.rkmathbangalore.org/public/images/thumbs/Govardhana%20Ma%E1%B9%ADha.jpg" alt="Govardhana मठ at पुरी">Govardhana मठ at PurīThe first pontiff of the गोवर्धन मठ at पुरी was पद्मपाद, one of the four chief disciples of शङ्कर, who is reputed to have rescued his गुरु from the clutches of the kāpālikas who wanted to sacrifice him.
The Veda assigned to this मठ is the Ṛgveda. The brahmacārins of this tradition are given the appellation ‘Prakāśa.’ ‘Vana’ and ‘Araṇya’ are the titles reserved for the saṁnyāsins ordained through this मठ.
There seem to be breaks in the continuity of the gurus occupying the pontiff’s seat.
See also DAŚANĀMĪS.
